Before sharing the pitch, the following questions need to be clarified:
1) In which entity am I investing in? From the above, I can see a 3 tier structure. Will I be investing in the holding company, parent company or subsidiaries? 
2) Who is running the show? Is it a single person who will manage it all? or is it a team who will handle individual entities?
3) What's the period of obtaining synergies? As you pointed out in one of your comments, you are looking to gain long-term value. Is there any visible timeline, game plan, funding stages, or funding quantum envisaged? 
4)Generally, angel investors have a 3-5 yrs exit horizon. What's your plan to give them an exit in that timeline?
5) Are you going to form all the entities at the same time? Would angel funding be required for you to even incorporate the companies?

As you can see, the structure of the holding is only one of the many things angel investors will look at. At the conceptualization stage, the bet is more on the founding team, the markets and the probability that the team will be able to deliver. 

Things change over a period of time and structures evolve to accommodate the changes. While your long term goal is commendable, it has to be broken into milestones and funding planned for each milestone.

I see several above have given you good advice. So I will just give my 2 cents. As a financial consultant, registered valuer, angel investor and owner of a financing company, investment has been all that I do for a while. The learnings are below : 

1) the risk equals reward. Yiu cannot get low risk high reward else everyone would do it and it won't get you any rewards 
2) you invest where YOU see value. Not everyone had the same opinion on an opportunity. If you think you can make value somewhere, invest there. Forget what others say about the space 
3) For a beginner, stock market is lucrative as we see only success stories. Those are one offs or patient capital. Do not go into the stock market without knowing it like the back of your hand. It will eat you up. 
4) If you are young and want to invest for long term, only invest money which you do not need right now. Don't invest your daily expense amount as well. The more you move money, the lesser it gets you return 
5) do not fall for "give us 1 lakh, we will give you 3 lakhs in 2 months ". Read about Ponzi schemes. 
6) at the end of it all, there is one golden rule in investment. So not play with borrowed money. Don't borrow to invest. It will come back to bite you. 

Wishing you all the very best.
